name: Manjeet Sandhu
conditions: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: initial assessment of hypothyroidism, allergic rhinitis and heart failure with reduced EF.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports fatigue, mild dyspnoea on exertion, nasal congestion and occasional sneezing.
EXAMINATION: BP 138/84 mmHg, weight 62 kg, height 1.58 m, BMI 24.8 (overweight). JVP not elevated, lungs clear, cardiac rhythm regular, S1S2 normal, no murmurs, abdomen soft, no edema.
IMPRESSION: 1) Hypothyroidism – TSH to be checked. 2) Allergic rhinitis – symptomatic. 3) Heart failure with reduced EF – NYHA class II. 4) Overweight – advise diet and activity.
ARRANGEMENTS: Start levothyroxine 50 mcg OD, cetirizine 10 mg HS, fluticasone nasal spray 1 spray each nostril OD, montelukast 10 mg HS. Initiate sacubitril/valsartan 24/26 mg BD, bisoprolol 2.5 mg OD, spironolactone 25 mg OD, furosemide 40 mg OD, dapagliflozin 10 mg OD. Order TSH, free T4, lipid profile, fasting glucose, serum K, creatinine, NT-proBNP and echocardiogram. Return if chest pain, worsening dyspnoea, fever >39°C, palpitations or sudden weight gain.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: routine follow‑up, review of thyroid and heart failure status.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient feels better, less fatigue, nasal symptoms controlled with cetirizine. No new dyspnoea.
EXAMINATION: BP 132/80 mmHg, weight 61.5 kg, BMI 24.6 (overweight). No edema, JVP normal, lungs clear.
IMPRESSION: 1) Hypothyroidism – TSH improved but still slightly high; increase levothyroxine. 2) Allergic rhinitis – well controlled. 3) Heart failure – stable, EF unchanged. 4) Overweight – reinforce diet and activity.
ARRANGEMENTS: Increase levothyroxine to 75 mcg OD. Continue other meds. Repeat TSH, free T4, lipid panel, fasting glucose, K, creatinine, NT-proBNP. Return if worsening dyspnoea, chest pain, palpitations, fever >39°C or sudden weight gain.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: increased ankle swelling and slight weight gain.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports 2‑kg weight gain over past month, bilateral ankle swelling, mild dyspnoea on walking uphill.
EXAMINATION: BP 138/86 mmHg, weight 63.5 kg, BMI 25.4 (obese). Mild pitting edema up to mid‑calf bilaterally, JVP not elevated, lungs clear.
IMPRESSION: 1) Hypothyroidism – TSH stable on current dose. 2) Allergic rhinitis – controlled. 3) Heart failure – fluid retention suggestive of worsening; consider diuretic increase. 4) Obese – reinforce diet, activity, consider weight‑loss referral.
ARRANGEMENTS: Increase furosemide to 60 mg OD, add spironolactone 25 mg BD (total 50 mg OD). Continue other meds. Order repeat electrolytes, creatinine, NT-proBNP, lipid profile and fasting glucose. Return if sudden weight gain >2 kg in 3 days, dyspnoea at rest, chest pain, or fever >39°C.
